court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Additional Mahila Court at Coimbatore, C.C.No.901 of 2020

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: C.Senthilkumar, C.Prema, Rukkumani, Ravi, R.Amutha, Nadarajan (husband/wife and others)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State rep.by The Inspector of Police, All Women Police Station, Perur, Coimbatore (government agency) and Asokadevi

facts_of_case: The case involves a complaint filed by the second respondent against the petitioners alleging harassment and dowry demands after her marriage to one of them. The trial court took cognizance for offences under Section 294(b), 498(A), 506(2) IPC and Section 4 of Tamilnadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, 2002.

legal_principles.principle: The knowledge of the first marriage and pendency of divorce petition is a ground to quash the proceedings.
legal_principles.held: Further he submitted that mere pendency of the divorce petition filed by the 1st petitioner and the private complaint filed by the 2nd respondent cannot be considered by this court under section 482 of Cr.P.C. It can be only considered during the trial before the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The knowledge of the first marriage and pendency of divorce petition is a ground to nullify the subsequent marriage.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, at the time of marriage between the 1st petitioner and the 2nd respondent on 01.06.2017, the 2nd respondent's 1st marriage was very much existing and as such marriage between the 1st petitioner and the 2nd respondent is null and void.

outcome.final_order: The final court order is to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.901 of 2020.

keywords: Tamilnadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act
